notes: SHIP v1.14.371 - SHIP 4: .tile state family retokenised + PORT MAP accent. Owner ruling 2026-08-03: teal to match, tile family only, split the rest; portmap rides ship 4. THE KEY FINDING: glow-normalisation and the R5 red/green purge were never two jobs - the .tile.* family paints its state channel AND its glow from the same declaration, so the state-to-channel mechanism 4b wanted ALREADY EXISTED and was simply wired to two off-palette tokens. Retokenising it closes both at once; no new helper was built. WHAT CHANGED (14 lines - 13 in the .tile family, 1 in DEPLOY_TOOLS): .tile.is-done fill/underline/rk-led/card-shadow go green to TEAL (var(--teal), glow rgba 31,255,208); .tile.is-blocked rk-led/border+shadow go red to MAG (#ff2bd6, glow rgba 255,43,214); DEPLOY_TOOLS PORT MAP ac #30d158 to #1fffd0. THE FAMILY IS 13 SITES, NOT 6 - AND STEP 0 GOT THAT WRONG. The first pass retokenised the six sites Step 0 had catalogued, then a residual-token assertion inside the .tile block flagged seven MORE carrying var(--red)/var(--green): a second .tile.is-blocked border rule, the blocked FILL and blocked UNDERLINE, .tile-flag, both .tile-pip states, and body.rd .tile-active-hdr .blk. Step 0 missed them because both of its greps were shaped by the symptoms already seen - one filtered for box-shadow (these have none) and one for literal hex (these use var() tokens). Shipping on that inventory would have produced a blocked tile with a MAGENTA led and border sitting on a RED fill and underline - visibly half-migrated, and worse than not shipping. The assertion caught it because it tested the BLOCK for residual tokens rather than testing that the planned edits applied. Lesson: assert the absence of what must be gone, not just the presence of what you changed. .tile.is-active was ALREADY correct cyan and is untouched. THE TRAP THIS SHIP IS BUILT AROUND: every glow is a hard-coded rgba(), not a var(), so changing the token alone would have left a green glow under a teal fill. Both halves moved on every line. Also two DIFFERENT reds were in play - .tile.is-blocked used rgba(255,45,85), NOT the #ff453a found everywhere else - so a pattern-match on #ff453a would have missed this entirely. RULE 7 CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: .tile is not body.rd-scoped, so legacy leak was a real risk. The three emitters (#tt-deploy/#tt-scan/#tt-handoff) were confirmed to live inside #pg-cmd and route via cmd_route() - redesign house only. ?legacy=1 untouched. PORT MAP now agrees with its own OPS wall cell (L13342, already teal) - that row had been disagreeing with the wall about the same tools channel. TOKEN STYLE mirrors the proven local precedent at #pg-cmd .cc-hdot / .cc-hdot.bad: var(--teal) for teal, literal #ff2bd6 for mag.
